meta.title_in_my_learning: ScholarClone: What is your school not seeing?
meta.audience: School promoters, trustees, principals, directors and academic leaders in India
owner_decisions: 2026-11-24 (current): every product is complete; no status label of any kind on a slide, clip or PowerPoint. The badge decisions below are superseded and kept as history.

2026-11-24: the explainer clips are motion graphics with made-up school data (a safe place to record the real product was not available); the web deck plays them live, the video files are for sharing.
Badges approved: Core LIVE; Learn, CCB, Insight, Compass PARTIAL; One CONCEPTUAL. Actual and planned functionality are always shown apart.
Wording corrected to match code: learning goal -> plan drawn from the diagnosis; CCB evidence -> ratings; Compass drops competencies.
Not used until independently verified: 'one login, nothing entered twice'; 'AI questions are reviewed before students see them'.
No customer named without explicit written permission.
Buyer claims only after a real recorded discovery call; never invented.
Real screenshots from an authorised environment; labelled placeholders until received.

Story direction approved (conditional) on 2026-11-23: every fact traceable; illustrative never shown as real; PARTIAL distinguished from LIVE; no unsupported marketing claims; existing G2G Sales Training untouched. Not yet approval of the rendered deck.
Slide 15 invitation wording approved. Slide 8 mastery-paths line removed until independently verified.

Discovery call arranged by the internal Sales/Management team; no invented feedback; explicit recording consent first. Screenshots only from an authorised staging/demo environment, personal data masked, source and licence register kept.

2026-11-24: all six products are presented as complete. No status labels (LIVE, PARTIAL, CONCEPTUAL) and no 'not built yet' panels appear anywhere a customer can see. A capability appears only when a file or a screen proves it; what the code review could not find stays in the presenter-only 'limits' of each slide.
meta.ship_rule: A slide may ship only when every 'fact' line cites a claim whose status is verified or owner-confirmed. No status badge, mark or banned word (partial, in progress, planned, conceptual, beta, coming soon, roadmap, prototype) may appear in customer-visible text. 'limits' are presenter-only.

slides.takeaway: The school promoter stops and asks what they are missing.

on_slide.text: What is your school not seeing?
Even when it has the data, the reports and the software.
Discover what becomes possible when your school starts connecting the dots.

slides.visual: A real photograph of a modern Indian classroom in soft morning light, slightly out of focus. A few fine points of light hover above desks; faint lines start between two or three points, then fade. The picture never fully resolves. No logo, no product name, no interface, no robot.
slides.motion: GSAP timeline: slow rack-focus between two depth planes; points of light appear, lines draw (DrawSVG) and dissolve before they connect. Headline words settle with SplitText, one beat apart. Meaning carried: something is there but not yet connected. Reduced motion: a still frame with the points visible and no drawing.
slides.say: Pause on the question. Do not explain anything. Let them answer first: what do you think a school like yours might not be seeing?
slides.ask: What would you say your school is not seeing today?
slides.transition: You already hold a lot of information. Let us look at where it comes from.

slots.brief: Modern Indian school classroom, students and teacher, natural light, shallow depth of field. Licensed photo; AI image only if the owner says yes.

slides.takeaway: The problem is often not missing data; it is data that has not been connected.

on_slide.text: What if the information your school already has could help you see more clearly?
The challenge is not always missing data. Sometimes it is connecting what you already have.

slides.visual: A real photograph of a principal at a desk, seen from behind or in profile, face not the focus. Eight labels sit around them as quiet paper-like tags.
slides.motion: GSAP: the eight tags drift in from their own depth and settle; a single thread then passes between two of them and holds. Meaning carried: the sources exist; connection is what is missing. Motion layout for the tag ring uses Motion (layout) so the ring re-flows on resize.
slides.say: Every school already produces all of these. Ask which of them the principal sees together on one day.
slides.ask: Which two of these do you look at side by side today?
slides.transition: Let us make this real with one student.

slots.brief: School principal at a desk in an Indian school office, not looking at camera. Licensed photo.

slides.takeaway: Recording a problem is not the same as knowing the next learning step.

on_slide.text: A student keeps struggling. The school has the records. What happens next?
Recorded: the problem is written down.
Understood: the gap is found, the next learning step is clear, and progress is reviewed.
Illustrative situation, to validate with you

slides.visual: A student at a desk with a notebook (real photograph, face turned away). Three record cards float beside the student. A fourth, empty card reads only a question mark.
slides.motion: GSAP Flip: the three cards slide together into one stack, then the stack splits into the two columns (Recorded / Understood), so the viewer sees the same records either left on a shelf or carried forward. Meaning carried: same information, two outcomes.
slides.say: Make clear this is an illustration, not a customer story. Ask them to recognise it, not to agree with us.
slides.ask: Does this happen in your school? What usually happens after the marks are in?
slides.transition: So what separates a record from a next step?

slots.brief: Indian school student writing in a notebook, face turned or hands only. Licensed photo.

slides.takeaway: Information becomes useful only when it moves through understanding to action and review.

on_slide.text: Where does your school's information stop today?
Which of these matters most to you?

slides.visual: One clean line with six nodes, large type, plenty of space. No architecture diagram, no AI imagery.
slides.motion: GSAP DrawSVG draws the line node by node as the presenter advances; each node lights only when its step is spoken. After the sixth, five chips appear (Motion AnimatePresence). Choosing a chip routes to the matching scenario (slides 14, 8, 10, 11, 12) and returns to this slide. Nothing is scored.
slides.say: Walk the line slowly. Then stop and ask where their information stops. Let the leader pick the chip; follow the leader, not the script.
slides.ask: Where does your school's information stop today? Which situation matters most to you?
slides.transition: Let us look at how a school can close that gap.

slides.takeaway: ScholarClone connects information, supports decisions and helps the school act.

on_slide.text: An integrated intelligent K–12 platform designed to help schools connect information, support better decisions and take meaningful action.
School Intelligence means helping a school understand what its information is telling it, where attention is needed and what action may be appropriate next.

slides.visual: ScholarClone logo ring from the brand assets (the product page's own embedded logo), set on a calm field in brand navy and blue. First appearance of the product name in the deck.
slides.motion: The opening line pattern from slide 4 closes into the logo ring (GSAP morph of the line into the ring). Meaning carried: the platform is the answer to the line you just saw.
slides.say: Only now introduce the name. Read the definition once in plain words. Tell them the deck will always mark what works today and what is ahead.
slides.ask: Does that match how you would describe what you need?
slides.transition: Here is how the pieces fit together.

slots.brief: ScholarClone logo ring extracted from the product page. Owner to confirm the file to use.

slides.takeaway: The whole story in 59 seconds, silent, with made-up school data.

on_slide.text: Illustrative motion graphics with made-up school data.

slides.visual: The film plays across the whole stage and starts by itself; a Replay button sits in the corner.
slides.motion: The film is the motion: nine beats, five kinds of transition.
slides.say: Let the film play: 59 seconds, no sound, the words are on the screen. It covers the question, the six products, how they work, who sees what, how they connect and what we would like to talk about.
slides.ask: Which part of that would you want to see first, in your own school?
slides.transition: Now the six products and how they fit together.
limits: The film is motion graphics with made-up school data, not a recording of the live product. Say so if asked; real recordings are shown in a demo session.

slides.takeaway: Six products around one idea, each with an honest status.

on_slide.text: Six products, one idea: see, decide, act.
Scholar One: Integrated Intelligent School Platform
Scholar CCB: Competence and Capability Intelligence
One intelligent platform connecting the entire school.

slides.visual: Core at the base as the foundation; Learn, CCB and Compass around it; Insight above; One drawn as a ring around all. Not six equal cards.
slides.motion: GSAP builds the diagram from the base up, one product per beat. Motion layoutId lets a tapped product expand into its own slide (7 to 12) and shrink back. Meaning carried: how the products relate and which are ready.
slides.say: Do not read all six. Say what each one is for in one phrase, then point at the badges: this is where we are honest about status.
slides.ask: Which of these would you start with if you had to choose one?
slides.transition: Start with the part that runs the school every day.

slides.takeaway: Each product explained in one short clip, with made-up school data.

on_slide.text: See it work, one product at a time
Motion graphics with made-up school data, one idea each.

slides.visual: A large 16:9 player on the left; the five product names on the right, the playing one highlighted.
slides.motion: Next moves to the next product; each clip plays once and rests on its outcome line.
slides.say: Each clip answers one question a school leader asks. Watch one, and tell me which question sounds like your school.
slides.ask: Which of these five questions do you hear most in your own school?
slides.transition: Now each product a little closer, starting with school operations.
limits: The clips are motion graphics with made-up school data, not recordings of the live product. Say so if asked; real recordings are shown in a demo session.

slides.takeaway: The everyday work of the school moves from registers into workflows.

on_slide.text: The everyday work of the school, off the registers and into workflows
Fees: collection, online payment through the school's payment gateway, and cheque reconciliation.
Attendance: daily student and staff attendance with reports.
Examinations: exam creation, marks entry and result reports.
Also: admissions, student records, staff payroll, and messages to parents.
School situation (typical, to validate): collection, registers and marks are kept by hand and compiled at the end.
What could become easier: a clearer picture of collection, absence and results without compiling by hand.

slides.visual: Three real screenshot frames (fees, attendance, marks entry) set in a device frame, with labelled placeholders until received. Never a fake interface.
slides.motion: Motion layout: three rows open one at a time to reveal today, challenge, what the product does, value. GSAP only animates the frame entrance. Meaning carried: one row at a time keeps attention on a single workflow.
slides.say: Pick the one workflow the leader cares about. Detail for the other four is in the notes and a supporting slide.
slides.ask: Where do you currently find out something has gone wrong in fees or attendance?
slides.transition: Operations tell you what happened. Learning shows what to do about it for a student.

slots.brief: Fee collection screen, demo data, authorised environment.
Student attendance marking screen, demo data.
Marks entry or report card screen, demo data.

slides.takeaway: From 'which students failed' to 'what each student should learn next'.

on_slide.text: From 'who failed' to 'what to learn next'
A diagnostic that finds weak concepts, a plan drawn from it, recommended content, adaptive practice and one clear next action.

slides.visual: A horizontal journey with seven steps, a student photograph at the start and a real diagnostic screenshot frame (placeholder) at the third step.
slides.motion: GSAP timeline follows one student's journey; a marker travels step to step on advance. Motion handles the step panel that opens under each marker. Meaning carried: the order of the learning loop and where the student is in it.
slides.say: In plain words: find what the student does not yet understand, plan from it, practise, check, then decide what comes next. Say clearly that students do not set their own goals in the product today.
slides.ask: How does a teacher find out today which concept a student is stuck on?
slides.transition: Teachers carry the rest of this load. Here is where AI helps them.

slots.brief: Diagnostic result with concept breakdown, demo student.

limits: Students do not set learning goals in the product: the plan is drawn from the diagnosis and is read-only.

slides.takeaway: AI helps teachers prepare; it does not replace them.

on_slide.text: Less time preparing, more time coaching
AI can draft questions and learning content for school staff to use.
Chapter content can become flashcards, true/false questions or a short presentation.
What could become easier: repeated preparation, more activity options for different learning needs, and more time to coach and mentor.
AI supports the teacher. The teacher stays in charge of the classroom.

slides.visual: A real photograph of a teacher with a small group of students, with a short before/after pair of generated items (an example question set) shown as a real screenshot placeholder.
slides.motion: Motion shared-layout: one chapter paragraph expands into three activity options and back. Meaning carried: one source, several forms.
slides.say: Keep it concrete: the teacher picks a chapter and gets drafts to adjust. Do not promise checking or approval steps until verified.
slides.ask: Which part of preparation takes most of your teachers' time today?
slides.transition: Teachers also need support to grow. Here is how that can be tracked.

slots.brief: Indian school teacher with small group of students, natural light. Licensed photo.
Question or content generation screen, demo data.

slides.takeaway: Staff development moves from occasional training to ratings, gaps, a plan and tracked progress.

on_slide.text: From occasional training to continuing development
Staff are rated on each competency, a gap view shows where they stand, and a development plan with actions can be updated.
Illustrative teacher situation, to validate with you

slides.visual: A real photograph of a teacher in a staff room or corridor. A six-step journey strip.
slides.motion: GSAP draws the journey; the 'Gap' step pulses once, the only place the strip pulses. Meaning carried: the gap is the pivot between knowing and developing.
slides.say: Use an unnamed teacher. Describe ratings, a gap view and a development plan with actions that can be updated.
slides.ask: How do you know today whether a training you ran changed what a teacher can do?
slides.transition: Everything so far produces signals. Leaders need them in one place.

slots.brief: Teacher in school corridor or staff room, Indian context, licensed photo.
Competency gap or development plan screen, demo data.

limits: No automatic suggestion of learning from a staff gap in schools. The Assign Learning button on the K-12 screen has no backend route: never click it in a demo.

slides.takeaway: Signals from different functions help a leader see where attention is needed, and a person decides.

on_slide.text: See where attention is needed. Decide. Review.

Signals from several functions, an attendance and results comparison across classes, and an academic-risk case that joins results, attendance and assignments. Recommendations wait for a person to approve or reject them.
This shows association between measures, not cause.
Illustrative case, to validate with you
One case, with a recommended action

slides.visual: A single case card (real screenshot placeholder), a hand over an approve / reject / defer choice. Not a dashboard wall.
slides.motion: GSAP: three signal threads converge into the case card; Motion AnimatePresence swaps the card between approve, reject and defer states. Meaning carried: three signals become one decision a person makes.
slides.say: This is decision support, not automation. Say the comparison shows a link, not a cause. Do not describe it as a forecast or as finding students early.
slides.ask: When a report arrives, who decides what happens next, and where is that recorded?
slides.transition: One more thread: where does a student's future fit in?

slots.brief: Academic-risk case with recommendation, demo data.

limits: On the academic case the screen offers approve and reject. A third choice (defer) exists in the backend and on the fee screen.

slides.takeaway: Career conversations can start from a student's interests and learning evidence.

on_slide.text: A career conversation that starts from evidence
Students can answer interest questions and a personality questionnaire, and record their aspirations and how sure they are.
An aspiration is compared with interests and learning evidence. When the evidence is thin, the result says so and does not guess.
This guides exploration. It does not forecast a student's career.
Illustrative situation, to validate with you

slides.visual: A real photograph of a senior-class student with a counsellor, neutral and warm. A screenshot frame for the alignment result (placeholder).
slides.motion: GSAP brings two circles (interests, learning evidence) together; the overlap shows the alignment result; if the circles stay apart a labelled 'not enough evidence' state shows instead. Meaning carried: honesty when evidence is missing.
slides.say: Lead with the honest part: when there is not enough evidence the product says so. Never say competencies or any career outcome.
slides.ask: What does career guidance look like for your senior classes today?
slides.transition: Now the part that matters most: how these connect.

slots.brief: Senior student with a school counsellor, Indian context, licensed photo.
Career alignment result screen, demo data.

limits: Career alignment depends on a graph service: confirm it is running before a demo.

slides.takeaway: Information from one part of the school reaches the others without being re-entered.

on_slide.text: A submitted online exam, and concepts a student masters in practice, are added to that student's career evidence automatically.
Attendance and results are compared across classes.
Results, attendance and assignments are joined into one risk case.

slides.visual: Four domains placed as a map and three solid connections. Clean line drawing, no glow, no network-of-nodes cliche.
slides.motion: GSAP DrawSVG: each connection draws once, then its number appears. Meaning carried: information moves from one part of the school to another.
slides.say: Show each of the three connections with its screen. Say plainly what each one does and what it needs.
slides.ask: Which missing connection would matter most to your school?
slides.transition: Let us put it in a day.
limits: Practice-to-career evidence needs at least 2 mastered concepts and a running queue worker. Staff capability is not connected to learning for school staff.

slides.takeaway: A principal's five questions already have answers in different places; one morning view is the next step.

on_slide.text: Scholar Insight's leadership overview brings health, what changed, what is at risk and priority actions onto one page.
Illustrative scenario, not a customer case

slides.visual: A real photograph of schoolgirls walking to school in the morning; five questions that each name the product holding the answer (Insight, Learn, CCB, Core, Insight).
slides.motion: Motion: each question expands to name the product that holds its answer. GSAP only runs the opening camera drift. Meaning carried: where each answer lives today.
slides.say: Let the principal choose one question and follow it to its product. Finish on the leadership overview.
slides.ask: Which of these five do you answer first on a normal morning?
slides.transition: If this feels worth testing, here is how we would start together.

slots.brief: Principal arriving at an Indian school in the morning, licensed photo.

scenarios.title: The principal's morning
scenarios.label: Illustrative
scenarios.situation: It is a quarter to eight. The principal has a few minutes before assembly and wants to know where to look first.
scenarios.challenge: Fees, attendance, results and staff matters sit in different places, so deciding where to look takes time.
scenarios.capability: Scholar Insight: signals from several functions, the leadership overview and risk cases; Scholar Core: fees and attendance reports.
scenarios.next_action: Open the cases waiting for a decision; ask the accounts head about the fee follow-up list; speak to one class teacher.
scenarios.value: The first hour can go to acting, not searching.

scenarios.title: A student who is struggling
scenarios.label: Illustrative
scenarios.situation: A Class 7 student has scored low in two tests in a row. The teacher has notes and a parent has called.
scenarios.challenge: The school has the marks and the concern but not a clear picture of which concepts need work.
scenarios.capability: Scholar Learn: a diagnostic by concept, a plan drawn from it, recommended content, adaptive practice and one next action.
scenarios.next_action: Start with the concepts marked weak; practise at the right level; use the next action after practice.
scenarios.value: The conversation with the parent can name specific concepts and a plan.

scenarios.title: A teacher who needs development
scenarios.label: Illustrative
scenarios.situation: A teacher and the head of department both rate the teacher lower on assessment design.
scenarios.challenge: A training day may have been held, but nobody can say whether that competency has changed.
scenarios.capability: Scholar CCB: ratings, a gap, a development plan with actions, and progress tracking.
scenarios.next_action: Agree two actions in a development plan; re-rate after the review date.
scenarios.value: Development is tied to a stated gap and followed up.

scenarios.title: A school leader making a difficult decision
scenarios.label: Illustrative
scenarios.situation: A director must decide whether to add remedial support for one grade next term.
scenarios.challenge: Opinions differ and the evidence is spread across attendance, results and teacher notes.
scenarios.capability: Scholar Insight: an attendance and results comparison across classes, and risk cases with a recommendation a person approves or rejects.
scenarios.next_action: Review the comparison and the cases; record the decision.
scenarios.value: The decision is made with evidence on screen, and the decision is recorded. The comparison shows a link, not a cause.

scenarios.title: A student exploring a future
scenarios.label: Illustrative
scenarios.situation: A senior-class student says they want a particular career but has not looked at their own interests or strengths.
scenarios.challenge: A counselling conversation has little evidence to start from.
scenarios.capability: Scholar Compass: interest profile, aspirations, and an alignment result that says so when the evidence is thin.
scenarios.next_action: Use the result to open the conversation; add evidence where it is thin.
scenarios.value: The conversation starts from evidence. Nothing is promised about the student's career.

asset_rules.photos: Real licensed photographs with source, licence and credit recorded in assets.json; AI-generated imagery only where the owner says yes, and recorded as such.
asset_rules.screenshots: Genuine ScholarClone screenshots from an authorised environment only; until received each slot shows a labelled placeholder. Never a fabricated interface.

asset_rules.swap: Every image is a slot id in assets.json so any one can be replaced without touching the slide.
